identity.name: Calcium lactate
identity.chemical_class: Organic acid salt (calcium salt of lactic acid)

function.mechanism: Acts as a calcium lactate buffer/salt for pH control and texture support, while also contributing calcium in fortified foods.

adi.basis: OpenEFSA record EFSA-Q-2011-00602 shows re-evaluation of E327 is ongoing and no finalized EFSA output/ADI is linked.

efsa.key_finding: Latest EFSA record for E327 re-evaluation is in Ongoing Risk Assessment (last modified 2026-01-19), with no final scientific output published in that record.

adi.basis: JECFA chemical page reports ADI as NOT LIMITED (qualitative, non-numeric).

concerns.summary: Regulatory caution exists for infant-related use contexts (FDA excludes infant foods/formulas; JECFA comment states D(-)-/DL-lactic acid should not be used in infant foods).
An in vitro 2023 study reported reduced endothelial cell viability for calcium lactate at higher concentrations; dietary relevance at normal food-use exposures is uncertain.

no_concern_confirmed: Two-year F344 rat study reported no treatment-related carcinogenic signal for calcium lactate (PMID: 1937289).
Subchronic F344 rat study reported no severe toxicological findings up to 5% in drinking water (PMID: 2636938).
FDA affirms calcium lactate as GRAS under 21 CFR 184.1207 with CGMP conditions.
JECFA lists ADI as NOT LIMITED for calcium lactate.

adi_exceedance.notes: Numeric ADI exceedance cannot be calculated from JECFA because ADI is qualitative (NOT LIMITED); risk boundary is mainly subgroup-based caution.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evidence indicates low concern at normal food-use levels (FDA GRAS and JECFA not-limited ADI), but EFSA re-evaluation for E327 remains unresolved and infant-related caution appears in both U.S. and JECFA records.
key_factors: EFSA E327 re-evaluation record is ongoing with no final output linked
FDA GRAS status under 21 CFR 184.1207 with CGMP use and infant-food/formula exclusion
JECFA ADI is NOT LIMITED (evaluation year listed as 1974)
No IARC listing found for calcium lactate in current classification dataset
Animal toxicology studies do not indicate strong carcinogenic/toxic signals at tested levels
